source: All women seem so guileless. Hardly any are truly as harmless as they seem.
They may seem like idle gossips, but there's steel in both of them. I'm keeping my distance.
Keep an eye out. My mutiny begins shortly.
About what?
I know about the plan you're hatching. The one to overthrow Grace.
How, exactly, can you know that?
You're not as opaque as you think you are.
I also suspect your contingency plan. You'd trade my life for Rosie and Guilda's if it came to it, wouldn't you?
Well, of course.
But if you've come here to dissuade me, you won't change my mind about that.
Prince Hamlet has a plan to retaliate against you violently. I'd be willing to share details...
Does he, now? Do tell.
I see. Fascinatin'. Thank yeh much, lady.
I've much respect for those whose hearts I can trust. I won' forget this.
I heard you speaking of your adventures. Can you... tell me more?
Certainly. Though I must admit, the bulk of my tales are to an audience.
I'll have to charge you a very steep price if you want a private story.
I've got a little coin on me—
I was talking about your company and private conversation. The attention of a fair woman is all the prize in the world.
I... that wouldn't be proper. We haven't even met before.
What's to know? I'm Othello, humble barkeep. And you, of course, are the lady Ophelia—I've seen your brother, too.
Why should the black sheep not flock together?
Ah... I didn't know I was so well-known.
Of course. And the subject of some mystery, too! Hardly anyone in town has laid eyes on you. And now I've met you for myself.
If the sad old tales of a washed-up sailor are of interest to one as fair as you, come see me at midnight, when the bar closes.
We'll speak further then.
I hear you've been beset by thugs as of late.
It would appear my fortune has quickly changed.
I was warned that the castle guard has decided to make their presence known in town, in order to protect me.
Rumor has it a young noblewoman pleaded my case to them. I wonder who that might be?
If you'd be so inclined, I'd like to speak with you in private later this evening.
Both to extend my deepest gratitude... and to get to know the fair woman to whom I owe my life and limb.
The bar closes at midnight. Meet me then.
I'll make do.
That wasn't what I asked. Haven't you asked the city guard for assistance?
You should well know, my lady, that the guard doesn't help people like us.
To them, we look better smeared beneath their heels.
I... Listen. I know some of them personally. Maybe they'll help me.
Othello the Barkeep seems to be in trouble.
Yes. It's been that way nearly ever since he moved here.
Vile insects that won't leave the poor man alone!
Their violence upon him is new, and I fear it will grow worse. But Castle Town is an outside world.
I do not meddle in its affairs, nor it in mine.
But don't you think there's some way we could help him?
Something-- anything?
The good Guard Captain may have the answer you seek.
Bernardo demonstrates remarkable softness whenever it comes to your requests.
Othello's in trouble. Can you help?
Me? What do you think I can do?
You could help defend his inn. I've seen you fight. You were a soldier once.
O-Ophelia, that isn't how this works.
I'm no Dane. I'm merely passing through. Inviting that kind of attention could be very dangerous for me.
Othello's a good man, and I care for him greatly, and he serves good wine, but...
But you're afraid to get involved.
Yes. And so should you be.
Othello's in trouble. Can you assist?
Oh, my, no. What do I look like to you? A personal army?
I've never even held a weapon before. It is my belief that the pointed side goes outwards...
But one can never truly be certain, can they?
I fear Othello will simply have to work out his woes on his own.
What would you like me to do?
Help me find someone who can make sure Othello's bar is defended.
Ah. Well. Allow me to share this helpful technique for doing just that.
Whenever I'm in need of assistance, I simply go to the most crowded location I can find.
Then I lie face down on the ground, and I scream.
It's had a one hundred percent success rate of people inquiring as to whether I need help.
I-- I don't think this is the kind of help they mean.
Really? I've never said 'yes' before, so I wouldn't know. The pure joy of the cry for help is enough for me.
Othello the Barkeep has been beset by thugs. He needs assistance from the Castle.
Wah! That sorry ol' man's twice a thug over himself!
The way I see it, innocent people in Castle Town are being threatened and have no recourse.
M'lady, we don't... ah... get involved in those kinds o' matters.
Marcellus, please. I'm begging you to get involved in this one. He needs help.
F-f-fine! Fine. Stop lookin' at me wiv those big green eyes! Yer just like yer damn mother!
Othello, the barkeep in town, has been beset by thugs. Can't you do anything?
We don't ordinarily have jurisdiction over the town.
I know Othello. He ought to ask his local guards for protection.
He's tried. None of them will stand by him.
And how did you hear about this man's case, exactly? How do you know Othello?
I... he... well...
Ophelia! You've been rummaging around in town alone? With that barkeep?
Well, now I'm obligated to send Marcellus down for your own safety, if you're making friends with criminals.
My lady, be aware you are making things very difficult for all of us.
Be safe. Please.
I will. You have my word. I just want to make sure he's all right.
My lord, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Do you bear me any ill will as a result?
Wah hah hah! No. I care not a whit what Hamlet feels on this front. His feelings don't factor in here.
In fact, I'm about to arrange a suitable match for him with Lady Birgitta.
We've been holding back on the betrothal because of the war effort, but we should move quickly now that we have reached tentative peace.
In fact, I was about to arrange a match between Hamlet and Lady Birgitta, before she proved herself a liar.
There are, of course, other suitable candidates in the wings.
None of them you, naturally.
Well, no, of course not. Right now, I trust you implicitly. How could I ever mean to do you harm?
I didn't think so.
My lady, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Do you believe the King finds me inconvenient?
What? No! Absolutely not!
Ophelia... it hurts my heart to hear you even suggest such a thing.
Please, don't take it as an offense that he disapproves of a union between you and my son.
He is trying to make the best match possible, and we have only one heir, after all. It can sometimes be an inscrutable process.
In fact, my husband is about to arrange a suitable match for him with Lady Birgitta.
He'll arrange for a meeting between them soon.
Brit, do you believe King Claudius truly wants me dead because of my prior relationship with Hamlet?
Since you know the truth about me -- No. Not a chance. Who told you that rubbish?
Well, you did, to my brother. Offhand.
Hmm. Did I? That was to persuade him, I think.
But no -- I don't believe that for an instant. Claudius is far too dull to play chess like that.
No, 'Feely, I have-- had, at least-- a special monopoly on wanting you dead.
I think you're safe for the time being. I seem to have lost my nerve.
Maybe. Maybe not.
Why? Is there something ominous happening in your personal life?
Something's got you looking over your shoulder? If so, do tell.
Hamlet, I believe your uncle may want me dead because of our 'history' together.
I fear he wishes to make a more appropriate match with you. Lady Brit, perhaps.
I fear he wishes to make a more advantageous match with you.
And... I'm an obstacle to that.
My father's ghost warned me of this. It told me Claudius was a killer.
My father's ghost appeared before me on the walls. It warned me about this. It told me Claudius was a killer.
I believe you, Hamlet.
And now you tell me my uncle intends to take your life, too.
It's... almost too much to bear.
Not while I live.
I'll not allow him to harm you.
This only adds conviction to my crime. I shall do the world a favor.
...I can see only blood ahead of me.
For now, let me play the part he expects of me. But soon, Ophelia, he'll be gone.
And then he'll trouble you no more. I swear it.
For my own sanity, I must find out if my mother knew of this. I have to know if she was complicit, too.
Father, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Couldn't this be cause for the King to harm me?
Why do you ask? Did something happen?
Do you have reason to believe you might be... harmed?
I've overheard a conversation implying that the King may want me dead.
Suggesting he would harm you feels inordinately strong, love. However...
You know how Hamlet feels about me. I'm worried the King may act against me because of that.
Yes. Brit has the same worry.
What makes you think this? Did Claudius say something to you?
No. But I heard something I wasn't meant to hear. Let's leave it at that.
If Claudius does intend to act, it won't be by his hand. He'll send someone else. Someone he can distance himself from.
Meet me in the guards' quarters. We both have friends there. Let us discuss the evidence further then.
You need to be careful, Ophelia. Asking questions might only draw more attention to yourself.
Please, leave this to me. I will investigate.
Exit POLONIUS.
Exit HAMLET.
Exit CLAUDIUS.
Exit GERTRUDE.
Exit LAERTES.
Exit BERNARDO.
Exit MARCELLUS.
Exit LADY BRIT.
Exit IRMA.
Exit HORATIO.
Exit ROSENCRANTZ.
Exit GUILDENSTERN.
Exit OTHELLO.
Exit QUINCE.
Hmmm. Nothing.
Clearly you need more practice. Run along and try that on someone else, why don't you?
Oho. Not a bad plan.
Alas, I am no pawn, and cannot be removed from play. Invalid move!
But I can hardly fault you. That's the first thing I would have tried, myself.
What on earth?
Ugh-- Waaah! What's happening?!
This cannot be real.
What was that? O-oh...
Ophelia? Did-- did you do that?
